provenance.notes: Seed shipped with engram, drawn from a probe pass against claude 2.1.222 and re-checked against that version's help on 2026-08-05: every flag claimed here exists, and --permission-mode accepts acceptEdits, auto, bypassPermissions, manual, dontAsk, and plan. There is deliberately no `default` among them, so the default authority role maps to the empty string and omits the flag rather than passing an invalid value. AUTHORITY, verified by canary 2026-08-05: read-only is `--permission-mode dontAsk --disallowedTools "Edit Write NotebookEdit"`. A child so configured READ a file successfully and REFUSED to create one, with the denial recorded in permission_denials, and wrote no plan file. Do NOT use `--permission-mode plan` for read-only: plan mode does not withhold writes, it REDIRECTS the child into writing a plan file under ~/.claude/plans and returning a planning stub instead of the requested work. That cost a whole 8-child review batch its output channel on 2026-08-05. Flag spellings were read from help, not probed, so nothing here is verified on THIS machine until you run `engram dispatch probe claude --model <M>`. Note that -p means print here and profile on codex, so a spec copied between providers is wrong in a way that runs. SUPPRESSION, measured 2026-08-05 on claude 2.1.222 with an identical prompt, reading cache_creation_input_tokens from --output-format json. Do NOT use --bare: it documents that Anthropic auth is strictly ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or apiKeyHelper via --settings and that OAuth and keychain are NEVER read, so on a subscription login it fails with `Not logged in`. It would also move billing to API credits, a different payment rail rather than merely a lower cost. --setting-sources is the right lever and it is strictly better here. Measured ladder: no flag = 36,888 cache tokens / $0.0751; `--setting-sources user` = 14,848 / $0.0325; `--setting-sources local` = 3,693 / $0.0126; `--setting-sources ''` (no sources at all) = 3,685 / $0.0127. This spec uses the EMPTY form: identical cost to `local`, but `local` still loads .claude/settings.local.json if a repo has one, so it merely reduces the child's config where the empty form determines it. A 10x context reduction with OAuth intact. The `user` rung is NOT sufficient for isolation: a child asked its codename under that setting answered with the parent operator's codename, because ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md pulls in engram identity. Under `local` it had none. MODEL NAMES, same date: asking for the alias `haiku` silently ran claude-sonnet-5 with a clean exit and a plausible answer -- the exact silent substitution positive verification exists to catch. The flag itself is fine with a full model id, so the values map here uses full ids only and role names (cheap/balanced/strong) rather than aliases.
